findings.problem: RouteWorkflow has no typestate enforcement. mark_sent can be called on any RouteWorkflow regardless of prior lifecycle, allowing invalid transitions such as marking unsent/unvalidated items as sent, double-sending, or reverting state.
findings.failure_mode: A caller constructs RouteWorkflow with status="new" and is_sent=false, calls mark_sent, and the item transitions to is_sent=true without ever having been validated. The domain invariant (validate before send) is silently violated.
findings.fix: Replace RouteWorkflow with a typestate enum or tagged struct where mark_sent only accepts a validated pre-sent variant. Define distinct types RoutePending, RouteValidated, and RouteSent with transitions enforced at the type level.

findings.problem: status field is pub status: String, allowing arbitrary string values ("sent", "SENT", "", "null", typos) that represent no valid domain state. mark_sent at line 10 directly assigns "sent" as a string literal.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status="SENT" or status="" and the system treats it as a valid route state. Comparisons like status == "sent" are case-sensitive and fragile. The status field encodes lifecycle state but cannot express the invariant that status must be one of a fixed set of values.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with pub status: RouteStatus where RouteStatus is an enum: pub enum RouteStatus { New, Validated, Sent }. All comparisons become exhaustive match; invalid states are compile-time impossible.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans. There is no mutual-exclusion or ordering invariant between them. They are redundant with status: String and contradict it.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously, or sets is_sent=true while status="new". The three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent) can represent contradictory states with no runtime or compile-time guard. This is the classic boolean blind spot: any combination of n booleans yields 2^n states, most of which are invalid.
findings.fix: Remove is_validated and is_sent entirely. Encode lifecycle in the typestate enum from the status fix. The enum variant itself carries the lifecycle information (e.g., RouteSent variant implies validated=true and sent=true, no separate booleans needed).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> can exist in contradictory combinations with is_sent and status. is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None is invalid. is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(...) is invalid.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent sets is_sent=true but does not set sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving it as None. A caller constructs RouteWorkflow with is_sent=false and sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(12345), representing a route that has a sent timestamp but is not marked sent. Both contradictions are silently permitted.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 into the typestate variant that owns it. Example: pub enum RouteState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. sent_at_epoch_ms only exists when in Sent state, making the contradiction impossible by construction.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive domain identifier. Any string is valid including empty, whitespace, excessively long, or non-identifier content. No validation, formatting, or length constraint is enforced.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets id="" or id="  " or id=repeat('a', 100000). These are indistinguishable from valid route IDs at the type level, leading to potential collisions, injection vulnerabilities, or memory exhaustion in downstream consumers.
findings.fix: Replace with pub id: RouteId where RouteId is a newtype: pub struct RouteId(String); with a smart constructor fn RouteId(s: String) -> Result<RouteId, RouteError> that validates non-empty, bounded length, and character constraints.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. RouteWorkflow fields are pub and directly assignable, so callers can construct invalid domain states without any parsing or validation layer. The mark_sent function at line 9-12 mutates status and lifecycle booleans directly instead of transitioning through a typed boundary.
findings.failure_mode: External callers, tests, or shell code construct RouteWorkflow with arbitrary field values, bypassing all domain invariants. There is no parse-once-into-trusted-values pattern. The core logic consumes raw primitives rather than validated domain types, violating the functional core / imperative shell boundary.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide smart constructors (e.g., RouteWorkflow::new(id: RouteId) -> Result<RouteWorkflow, RouteError>) and domain methods that return Result/typed errors. Move raw construction into shell code that parses once at the boundary. Replace mark_sent with a method that returns a new typed variant rather than mutating in place.

residual_risk: Review is source-only. No commands were run. The code violates six independent Holzman + Functional Rust absolute laws: no typestate enforcement, no status enum, no lifecycle typestate, contradictory Option state, raw primitive ID, and missing parse boundary. All six findings are BLOCKER severity. The route workflow struct as written can represent every illegal state, and mark_sent mutates state directly without any domain invariant checks. Delivery is blocked until all six findings are resolved.
